…one (#142)

A stuck AVAudioEngine input node or start blocked the mic queue for good,
so the Dictation sat in "finishing" with no row and no outcome. The start
now races a deadline on MicHardware's clock: past it the Dictation fails
with a notice and a failed row, the stuck lane is abandoned, and the next
fn-down builds on a new queue. A late engine from the stuck lane is stopped.
The History row is recorded at fn-down in parallel with the mic start.

Live checks: macOS held the first start after a permission reset until
Jake answered its Allow prompt, so that Dictation hit the 2 s limit. The
limit now re-arms while the permission is undetermined, up to 60 s.

A file that can't be read is not a Dictation: no row, status nil, so
lexicon-eval still prints "nothing" and exits 1, and its path stays out
of the log. Fake mics default to a clock that never moves, and every
wedged test start is released even when an expectation fails.

fix(audio): ask for the mic before building an engine, and remember t…

…he answer (#142)

Live checks: after a re-grant every engine started cold, so the permission
macOS reports stayed "undetermined" after Jake clicked Allow. With the
previous commit's prompt allowance, every later start would have waited
up to 60 s, which is the post-re-grant wedge this ticket is about.

When the permission reads undetermined, fn-down now asks for it first
(AVAudioApplication.requestRecordPermission, up to 60 s for Jake to
answer), then gives the engine its 2 s. Jake's answer is kept for the
process, so a stale report neither keeps engines cold nor lifts the limit.
A late engine on an abandoned lane is not started. Fake wedges count
engine starts, not engines made.
